title: Roadside Breakdown Assistance — Bundled Bank Benefit, Overseas
goal: A customer whose vehicle has broken down overseas reaches assistance through a benefit bundled with their bank account, establishes their location, and gets the vehicle recovered to a garage able to repair it, with everyone safely onward
summary: A service mission mapped from the vantage point of the bank that bundles roadside assistance into a paid premium account. The bank owns the relationship and the benefits app; the assistance provider is a contracted partner; recovery, repair and hire vehicles are delivered by parties further removed still. The graph is deliberately drawn around a case that switches channels repeatedly — app to phone, phone back to app, app to phone again, then SMS, a third-party location service, a partner tracking site, and finally a messaging channel — because channel switching is where this service's design is actually tested.

scope.trigger: A vehicle the customer is travelling in breaks down, away from home and outside their own country
scope.completion: Vehicle delivered to a garage able to repair it, with all occupants safely onward
scope.timeframe: Roughly 24-48 hours from breakdown to vehicle delivered to a repairing garage; the wider case (repair, hire vehicle, vehicle return) runs for longer

successCriteria.metric: Time from first contact to location established
Proportion of cases where location is captured on the first method offered
Time from location established to recovery arriving
successCriteria.target: Within the quoted window on 90% of cases

successCriteria.metric: Proportion of customers who know the benefit exists before they need it
Contacts required per case after dispatch

actors.role: vehicle owner and decision-maker, never contacted by the service

phases.name: Cover in Place
phases.goal: The customer holds the benefit and knows it exists before they ever need it

phases.name: Breakdown & First Recourse
phases.goal: Everyone is safe and the customer works out who to call

phases.name: Reaching the Service
phases.goal: Get through to someone or something that can dispatch help

phases.name: Establishing Location
phases.goal: Get a location the service can dispatch to, by any means that works

nodes.name: Hold a premium account with bundled benefits

laneContent.description: The customer holds a paid premium current account. Roadside assistance is one of several bundled benefits, alongside things like cinema tickets and travel cover. The cover follows the person rather than a vehicle — it applies to any car they travel in, at home or abroad.

channels.name: Bank benefits app
channels.usageContext: Separate from the main banking app; the customer's route to every bundled benefit

channels.name: Benefit reminder emails
channels.usageContext: Periodic reminders of what the account includes

laneContent.frontstage: Benefits presented at account opening; a benefits app listing everything included; occasional reminder emails.
laneContent.backstage: Bank contracts with an assistance provider to deliver the benefit. Eligibility is tied to account tier and checked at the point of claim, not continuously.
data-required: Entitlement record shared with the assistance partner

kpis.metric: Benefit awareness among eligible customers
Benefits app monthly active use

significance.description: The entitlement exists from this moment, but is worth nothing unless the customer remembers it at the roadside. Everything downstream depends on awareness built here.

laneContent.description: The benefits app home screen lists everything included, so any visit for one benefit exposes the others. SCHEMA LIMITATION: this is not a step — it is an always-available surface with no position in a sequence. Modelling it as a node between account opening and discovery implies an ordering and a causation that did not exist. See prediction 1.

channels.name: Bank benefits app home screen
channels.usageContext: Always available; lists all bundled benefits regardless of why the customer opened it

channels.name: Concierge number printed on the bank card
channels.usageContext: SCHEMA LIMITATION: always in the wallet, reachable at any point in any journey. A standing capability, not a step. See prediction 1.

barriers.description: Awareness depends on the customer choosing to look. The surface is passive: it rewards curiosity but does nothing for a customer who visits, claims one benefit, and leaves.

designOpportunities: Surface the most situationally relevant benefit rather than a flat list
Prompt awareness ahead of known travel, using data the bank already holds
Make the concierge number reachable from the app, not only from the physical card
laneContent.frontstage: Benefits app home screen listing all included benefits; a concierge number printed on the card itself.
laneContent.backstage: Entitlement register drives what appears in the list. No triggering logic — the list is static regardless of customer circumstance.

kpis.metric: Benefits browsed per app visit
Customers who can name their roadside cover unprompted

significance.description: The only awareness mechanism in this service that actually worked — and it worked passively, as a side effect of a visit made for something else entirely.

nodes.name: Notice the roadside cover while claiming something else

laneContent.description: The customer visits the benefits app to claim an unrelated benefit and browses the rest of the list while there, noticing roadside assistance. SCHEMA LIMITATION: this happened weeks earlier, during a different journey, with no causal link to the breakdown. The graph can only place it immediately before the trigger, which invents a proximity and a sequence that did not exist. See prediction 6.

channels.name: Bank benefits app
channels.usageContext: Opened to claim an unrelated benefit; roadside cover noticed incidentally while browsing

barriers.description: Whether the customer knows about the cover at the moment of need is left to chance — it depends on having browsed recently enough to remember, for reasons unconnected to driving.
Noticing the benefit exists is not the same as knowing what it covers. The customer knew it existed but not that it followed them into any vehicle, or across Europe.

designOpportunities: Treat incidental browsing as the primary awareness channel it evidently is, and design for it deliberately
Record which benefits a customer has viewed, and refresh awareness before it decays
State the two facts that decide whether someone calls: which vehicles are covered, and where
laneContent.frontstage: Benefit list; a roadside assistance entry summarising what is included.
laneContent.backstage: No tracking of which benefits are viewed, so the bank has no signal about who is aware of what.

kpis.metric: Benefit detail views per active customer per year
Recall of roadside cover 3 months after viewing

significance.description: Without this incidental visit the customer would not have called at all, and the service would never have been used. The single most load-bearing node in the map, and entirely a matter of luck.

laneContent.description: The vehicle stops and cannot continue, on a journey away from home and outside the customer's own country. The group splits: some continue in a second vehicle, and the cover holder stays with the vehicle owner.

barriers.description: The breakdown is outside the customer's country, where local knowledge, language, and any home-market service relationship are all absent.

laneContent.frontstage: None — the service has no awareness that anything has happened.
laneContent.backstage: None. No telematics, no connected-vehicle signal, no proactive detection. The service learns of the incident only when the customer initiates contact.
designOpportunities: Detect breakdowns proactively where the vehicle or a connected app can signal them
Prompt the benefit at the moment of need rather than waiting to be remembered
roles-involved: None at this point — the service is unaware

kpis.metric: Time from breakdown to first contact with the service

significance.description: The trigger. Note the service is blind here — every second until first contact is unmeasured and unmanaged.

laneContent.description: Occupants move themselves and, where possible, the vehicle to a safe position before doing anything else. Part of the group leaves in a second vehicle to continue the journey.

barriers.description: Everything that follows happens outdoors, at the roadside, on a shared and finite phone battery, with whatever mobile signal is available. These constraints are situational rather than permanent, and shape every channel choice from here on.

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: Which cover applies to this vehicle, in this country, and what the service will need in order to find you
cognitive.supportAvailable: None. This step happens before any contact with the service, so there is no guidance of any kind.

designOpportunities: Lead every contact with a safety check, before identity or entitlement
Design location capture for weak signal, not for ideal conditions
laneContent.frontstage: None — this happens before contact.
laneContent.backstage: None.
roles-involved: None at this point — the service is unaware

kpis.metric: Cases where safety is confirmed within the first minute of contact

significance.description: Establishes the situational constraints — weak signal, no address, finite battery — that go on to defeat two of the service's three location methods.

laneContent.description: The vehicle owner contacts his own motor insurer first, as the obvious route. They refuse: he had not separately notified them of overseas travel, despite holding cover purchased for the specific trip dates. This is a different organisation entirely, outside the bank's service, but it is what routes the customer to the bundled benefit.

channels.name: Vehicle owner's own motor insurer
channels.usageContext: SCHEMA LIMITATION: no relationship to the bank at all, yet 'third_party' is the same value its partner's suppliers get. See prediction 2.

barriers.description: Cover bought for the exact trip dates is refused for want of a separate travel notification. The customer's preparation was substantively correct and procedurally incomplete, and the policy treats those as the same thing.
Neither refusing insurer nor customer checks for adjacent cover. Nobody asks whether another policy in the household might apply; the customer has to remember unaided.

designOpportunities: Prompt customers to check bundled benefits when a primary claim is refused
Make the bundled benefit discoverable at the moment another provider says no
laneContent.frontstage: A refusal delivered by phone, by an organisation outside this service.
laneContent.backstage: None visible to this service. The bank and its assistance partner learn nothing about the refusal, and never will.

kpis.metric: Cases reaching the bundled benefit only after another provider refused

significance.description: The bundled benefit was second choice, reached only because another provider refused. The service has no visibility of this and no way to be present at the moment it matters.

nodes.name: Remember the bundled cover might apply

laneContent.description: The cover holder recalls that his bank account includes roadside assistance and that it follows him rather than a vehicle, so it should apply to his brother's car abroad. He suggests trying it. This recall depends entirely on the incidental browsing weeks earlier.

barriers.description: The decision rests on remembering two specific facts — that the cover exists, and that it covers any vehicle anywhere in Europe. A customer who recalls only the first may not think it applies to someone else's car.

designOpportunities: Make 'does this apply to my situation?' answerable in seconds, at the point of recall
Push the benefit to customers whose circumstances suggest they may need it
laneContent.frontstage: None — this happens in the customer's head, unaided.
laneContent.backstage: None.
roles-involved: None at this point — the service is still unaware

kpis.metric: Eligible customers who consider the benefit at the point of need

significance.description: The gate for the entire service. Everything downstream is contingent on a memory formed for unrelated reasons, at a moment nobody designed.

laneContent.description: The customer opens the bank's benefits app at the roadside and navigates to the roadside assistance section. This is the bank's own channel and the only part of the journey it directly controls.

channels.name: Bank benefits app
channels.usageContext: Opened at the roadside on mobile data to find the roadside assistance entry

barriers.description: Requires working mobile data at the roadside. The same weak signal that will shortly defeat location capture also has to carry app loading and authentication.

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: That the benefit exists and lives in this app rather than the main banking app
cognitive.supportAvailable: Benefit list and search within the app; no contextual help for an active emergency

designOpportunities: Detect that the customer is abroad and surface travel-relevant benefits first
Allow the roadside section to load and function on a poor connection
Offer a single tap to contact, rather than a section to be navigated
laneContent.frontstage: Benefits app home screen; a roadside assistance section reached by browsing or search.
laneContent.backstage: App authenticates the customer against the core banking platform and checks account tier for entitlement. No case is created at this point — the bank's involvement ends at handing over contact details.

kpis.metric: Roadside section load time on a poor connection
Taps from app open to contact details

significance.description: The last node the bank owns outright. From here the customer passes to a partner, and the bank's visibility of its own benefit effectively ends.

laneContent.description: The roadside assistance section summarises what the cover includes and presents contact details. This is where the customer confirms the cover applies to a vehicle they do not own, in another country — the two facts the whole decision rests on.

channels.name: Roadside assistance benefit page
channels.usageContext: Summary of cover plus contact options, presented in the bank's own app

channels.name: Assistance provider website
channels.usageContext: SCHEMA LIMITATION: a usable route that exists but is never signposted here. Nothing distinguishes an available channel from a discoverable one. See prediction 3.

barriers.description: The customer must work out, under pressure, whether cover that follows a person extends to someone else's vehicle abroad. A summary written for browsing is being read as a decision aid in an emergency.
The provider's website is a working route to help and is not mentioned at the one moment it would be used. The customer only ever learns of the app and the phone numbers.

designOpportunities: Answer 'does this apply to me, right now?' before listing what is included
Signpost every route to help, including the provider's own website
Show the overseas number first when the customer is demonstrably overseas
laneContent.frontstage: Cover summary; contact details for domestic and overseas numbers; a prompt to install the provider app.
laneContent.backstage: Static benefit content maintained by the bank under contract with the provider. Not personalised to location, vehicle, or circumstance.

kpis.metric: Customers who correctly identify whether cover applies
Time from opening the section to initiating contact

significance.description: Where an unsignposted third route to help stays invisible. The customer chooses between two options believing they are the only two.

laneContent.description: The service presents two routes simultaneously — install the provider's app, or call, with separate domestic and overseas numbers. Both are genuinely offered and either can be taken. This is a service-offered fork, not a customer deliberation.

channels.name: Assistance provider app
channels.usageContext: Offered as the first option for raising a case; requires installation before it can be used

channels.name: Overseas assistance number
channels.usageContext: Offered for customers calling from outside the home country

channels.name: Domestic assistance number
channels.usageContext: Offered for customers calling from within the home country

barriers.description: Nothing indicates which route is faster or more reliable in the customer's actual situation. The choice is made on a guess, and the guess turns out to matter a great deal.
The app route requires a download and setup before it can do anything, at a roadside, on weak signal. The cost of that route is invisible at the point of choosing it.

designOpportunities: Recommend a route based on signal strength, location and case type rather than presenting a flat choice
State what each route will require before the customer commits to it
Let the app raise a case without installation, through the browser
laneContent.frontstage: Two contact options presented side by side: install the app, or call one of two numbers.
laneContent.backstage: No routing logic. The same options are shown to every customer regardless of circumstance, and no signal is passed to the provider about which was chosen.

kpis.metric: Cases raised by app versus phone
Customers who switch route after choosing

significance.description: The only genuine branch in the map — two channels offered at once, with no guidance on which suits the situation. The customer picks the phone on instinct, and is then pushed back to the app.

laneContent.description: The customer calls the overseas number, judging a person faster than an app install. The call reaches the provider's contact centre through a bank-specific route, so the agent knows which bank's customer they are supporting.

channels.name: Bank-specific overseas assistance line
channels.usageContext: A dedicated number for this bank's customers. Reliably answered quickly, and the agent knows which bank's benefit is being claimed.

barriers.description: An international call from a mobile at the roadside, on a shared and depleting battery, with an interactive menu to navigate before reaching a person.

designOpportunities: Offer a call-back so the customer is not holding an international call on a finite battery
Skip the menu entirely on the bank-specific line, where the benefit is already known
laneContent.frontstage: Interactive menu, then a contact centre agent who already knows which bank's benefit applies.
laneContent.backstage: Dedicated inbound routing per partner bank means entitlement is pre-established. Agent opens a case record in the provider's system; the bank sees none of this.
data-required: Inbound number dialled, which identifies the partner bank

kpis.metric: Time to answer on partner-specific lines
Cases where entitlement is confirmed without customer effort

significance.description: The dedicated partner line works well and is the one piece of the partner relationship the customer can feel. It is also the thing the agent then talks them out of using.

nodes.name: Agent suggests using the app instead

laneContent.description: Mid-call, the agent suggests it would be easier to use the app or the website. The customer abandons a working, answered call and installs the app. No case is created before the call ends, so nothing is carried forward.

channels.name: Bank-specific overseas assistance line
channels.usageContext: The call during which the customer is directed to a digital channel and then ends the call

barriers.description: Deflection to digital happens with no state carried across. The call ends without a case, so when the digital route fails the customer restarts from nothing — new call, new menu, identity confirmed again.
The deflection optimises for contact-centre cost in a situation where the customer has already judged the phone to be the faster route, and where the app's dependencies cannot be met.

designOpportunities: Never deflect without first creating the case, so a failed deflection costs nothing
Check whether the digital route can actually work here before recommending it
Let the agent stay on the line while the customer tries the app
laneContent.frontstage: Agent suggesting the app or website would be easier.
laneContent.backstage: Channel deflection guidance in agent scripting, aimed at reducing call handling time. No mechanism to persist a partial case across the switch.
data-required: Nothing retained — the call ends without a case record

kpis.metric: Deflected contacts that succeed digitally without a return call
Average handling time
kpis.target: Reduced — the intent behind the deflection

significance.description: The single most costly decision in the map. A working channel is abandoned on the service's advice, for a channel that cannot function in this situation, with no state carried across.

laneContent.description: The customer downloads and opens the provider's app at the roadside. It installs quickly. Raising a case requires no login — only entering some details — which is a genuinely good decision for an emergency.

channels.name: Assistance provider app
channels.usageContext: Installed at the roadside. Raising a case needs no account — details are entered directly.

barriers.description: An app download over weak mobile data, on a depleting shared battery, at the moment help is most needed. The install succeeded here; on a worse connection it would not have.

designOpportunities: Offer the same no-login case creation through a browser, removing the install entirely
Preinstall or deep-link the provider app from the bank's benefits app ahead of travel
laneContent.frontstage: App store download; app opens straight to case creation with no account required.
laneContent.backstage: Anonymous case creation path in the provider's platform, identified later by phone number rather than by account.

kpis.metric: App install to case created
Case creation abandonment rate

significance.description: No-login case creation is the right call for an emergency. It is undone at the very next step by a location requirement the customer cannot satisfy.

laneContent.description: The app asks for a postcode or offers to use GPS. Abroad there is no postcode for the location, and the signal is too weak for a GPS fix. Both options fail, and the app offers no third way. The case cannot be raised.

channels.name: Assistance provider app location capture
channels.usageContext: Offers postcode entry or GPS. Neither works at a European roadside on weak signal, and no alternative format is accepted.

barriers.description: Location capture offers exactly two methods and both depend on conditions a roadside breakdown routinely breaks — a postcode that only exists in the home country, and a GPS fix that needs signal.
A home-market assumption embedded in an app sold on overseas cover. Postcode entry is meaningless in the country where the cover is being claimed.
No fallback. When both methods fail the app has nothing else to offer and no route back to a human, so the customer is dropped entirely.

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: How to describe a location abroad in a format the app will accept, when it accepts only two and neither is available
cognitive.supportAvailable: None. No alternative format, no fallback, and no route from the failure back to a person.

designOpportunities: Accept any location format the customer can produce — coordinates, what3words, a shared pin, a description
Never present postcode entry as an option outside the country it exists in
Offer a route back to a human at the point of failure, carrying whatever has been entered
Degrade gracefully to a coarse location and refine it later, rather than blocking on precision
laneContent.frontstage: A location step offering postcode entry or GPS, with no third option and no way past it.
laneContent.backstage: Dispatch requires a resolvable location before a case can be created. The postcode path assumes a domestic incident; the GPS path assumes usable signal. Neither assumption holds here.
data-required: A resolvable location, in one of exactly two accepted formats

kpis.metric: Location capture success rate in-app
In-app location success on overseas cases
kpis.target: Currently unmeasured — this failure mode is invisible to the provider

significance.description: The deflection's cost lands here. The customer has given up a working call for a channel that cannot proceed, and the app has no way to hand them back.

nodes.name: Call back and re-enter the menu

laneContent.description: With the app unable to proceed, the customer calls the number again — new call, menus again, agent again. Nothing from the previous call or the app attempt carries over. This node opens the location-capture loop: the service will now try several methods in turn, all within this one call.

channels.name: Bank-specific overseas assistance line
channels.usageContext: Second call. The interactive menu must be navigated again and identity re-established from scratch.

barriers.description: No state persists across the deflection. The earlier call created no case and the app attempt left no record, so the customer starts from zero for the second time.
The interactive menu is presented again to a customer the service has already spoken to minutes earlier about the same incident.

designOpportunities: Recognise a repeat caller within a short window and route straight to a person
Persist any partial case from an abandoned app attempt and attach it to the next contact
Create the case at first contact, so a failed deflection costs the customer nothing
laneContent.frontstage: Interactive menu, hold, then an agent with no knowledge of the previous contact.
laneContent.backstage: No linkage between the abandoned call, the app session, and this new call. Each is an independent contact in the provider's systems.
data-required: Nothing carried forward — the customer supplies everything again

kpis.metric: Repeat contacts within 30 minutes for the same incident
Contacts where prior context is recognised and reused

significance.description: Opens the location loop. Also the point where the deflection's cost becomes concrete and measurable — a second full contact for one incident, caused entirely by the service's own advice.

laneContent.description: The agent's first question is whether the customer is in a safe location. This comes before identity, entitlement, or any commercial consideration, and it is the clearest example of the service being well designed.

channels.name: Bank-specific overseas assistance line
channels.usageContext: Agent opens with a safety check before anything administrative

designOpportunities: Keep this first, and protect it from any future attempt to front-load identity or entitlement
Mirror the same check in the app, which currently asks about location before safety
laneContent.frontstage: Agent asking directly whether the customer and passengers are somewhere safe.
laneContent.backstage: Safety triage is scripted ahead of case administration. A negative answer escalates to emergency services rather than continuing the assistance flow.
data-required: Whether occupants are in a safe position

kpis.metric: Contacts where safety is confirmed before administrative questions

significance.description: The service at its best. Worth recording alongside the failures — a well-sequenced human step that the digital channel does not replicate.

laneContent.description: The agent confirms the customer's name, address and account details to establish entitlement under the bank's benefit. Being the second call, this is the second time it has been done for one incident.

channels.name: Bank-specific overseas assistance line
channels.usageContext: Verbal confirmation of name, address and account details to establish entitlement

barriers.description: Identity is verified again because the previous contact left no record. The customer supplies from memory, at the roadside, details already given minutes earlier.
Full identity verification is required before dispatch on a case where entitlement was already established by the inbound number dialled.

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: Account details recalled from memory, without access to paperwork or a banking app on a low battery
cognitive.supportAvailable: Agent will prompt and accept partial answers, but the details must come from the customer

designOpportunities: Treat the partner-specific inbound number as sufficient for entitlement, and verify identity after dispatch
Send a verification link rather than requiring recall at the roadside
Never verify twice for one incident
laneContent.frontstage: Agent asking for name, address and account details.
laneContent.backstage: Entitlement checked against the partner register shared by the bank. The bank sees no record of this check.
data-required: Entitlement status under the partner benefit

kpis.metric: Time spent on identity verification per case
Cases requiring verification more than once

significance.description: Administrative work performed before the service knows where the customer is — the ordering the app got right and the phone route gets wrong.

laneContent.description: The agent sends an SMS containing a link that captures the device's location when opened. The message arrives, but the signal is still too weak for a fix. A second location method fails, this time on a different channel from the first.

channels.name: Location-capture SMS link
channels.usageContext: Agent-triggered link that reports device location back to the case. Delivered successfully; the location fix itself failed.

barriers.description: The second location method depends on the same underlying capability as the first — a usable position fix on a device with weak signal. Offering it after GPS failed adds a channel but not a genuine alternative.
No method offered so far accepts a location the customer could supply by other means. Every route requires the device to determine its own position.

designOpportunities: Offer methods that fail independently, rather than three routes to the same GPS fix
Accept a location relayed from a second device, which the customer very often has
Let the customer describe a location in words and geocode it agent-side
laneContent.frontstage: An SMS with a link; a page that attempts to read the device location and cannot.
laneContent.backstage: Link generation tied to the open case. On success the coordinates attach automatically; on failure there is no fallback path and the agent must improvise.
data-required: A device position fix — which is exactly what is unavailable

kpis.metric: SMS location link success rate
Cases requiring a third location method

significance.description: The second of three attempts at one task. Notable because it looks like a fallback but shares the dependency that broke the first attempt.

nodes.name: Customer researches what the service accepts

laneContent.description: The vehicle owner suggests a third-party location service. Before offering it, the customer runs a search to check the assistance provider supports that format — then proposes it to the agent. The customer researches the service's own capabilities, using a channel the service has no relationship with.

channels.name: Public search engine
channels.usageContext: SCHEMA LIMITATION: a channel wholly outside the service, used to establish what the service supports. Nobody in the chain owns or knows of it. See prediction 5.

barriers.description: The service never states which location formats it accepts. The customer has to discover a supported capability by searching the public internet, mid-call, while the agent waits.
The agent did not offer this method. The capability existed and went unmentioned until the customer raised it, so the resolution depended on the customer knowing to ask.

designOpportunities: State plainly which location formats are accepted, in the app, on the call, and in the SMS
Have agents offer alternative formats as soon as the primary method fails
Treat 'what does this service accept?' as a question the service should answer, not the customer research
laneContent.frontstage: None provided by the service. The customer uses a search engine and a family member's suggestion.
laneContent.backstage: The provider does support this format. Nothing surfaces that fact to the customer or prompts the agent to offer it.
support-systems: A second device belonging to another person
data-required: Knowledge of which location formats the provider accepts — held by the provider, discovered by the customer
roles-involved: None — the customer performs this unaided

kpis.metric: Cases where the customer proposes the method that resolves location
kpis.target: 0% — the service should offer it first

kpis.metric: Agent awareness of supported location formats

significance.description: The service's capability was known to the internet and not to its own agent. The customer bridged that gap using a channel nobody in the delivery chain owns.

nodes.name: Location relayed from a second device

laneContent.description: The vehicle owner obtains a precise location from a third-party service on his own phone, and the customer reads it aloud to the agent. The third method succeeds — on a different person's device, via a service the provider does not own, spoken over the phone. The location loop closes and the case can proceed.

channels.name: Third-party precise-location service
channels.usageContext: SCHEMA LIMITATION: supplied on the vehicle owner's device, not the caller's. Nothing records that a channel was used by a different person. See prediction 5.

channels.name: Bank-specific overseas assistance line
channels.usageContext: The location is read aloud and typed in by the agent — a verbal relay between two digital systems

barriers.description: Two digital systems exchange a precise location by being read aloud and retyped, because no direct route exists between them. Accurate here, but a transcription error would send recovery to the wrong place.
Resolution depended on a second person being present with a charged phone and better signal. A customer alone at the roadside would still be stuck.

designOpportunities: Accept third-party location formats directly in the app and on the web link
Allow a location to be submitted from any device against a case reference
Confirm a relayed location back to the customer to catch transcription errors
laneContent.frontstage: Agent accepting a spoken location reference and confirming it back.
laneContent.backstage: Agent enters the reference into the case, which resolves it to coordinates for dispatch. The provider does support the format — it simply never offered it.
data-required: A precise location reference in a supported format
A second device with signal — unacknowledged by the service as a dependency

kpis.metric: Total time from first contact to location established
Location methods attempted per case

significance.description: Closes a loop of three attempts across three channels. The method that worked was proposed by the customer, ran on someone else's phone, and belonged to a company with no relationship to anyone in the delivery chain.

condition.description: Own insurer refuses — no travel notification on file
Customer decides the bundled cover may apply and tries it
Customer judges a phone call faster than installing an app
Customer takes the app route offered alongside the phone numbers
Agent moves the customer to a digital channel mid-call, without creating a case first
Digital route cannot proceed; customer returns to the phone with nothing carried over
Second location method fails — device still cannot obtain a position fix
Designed retry cycle — on failure, return to the top of the location loop and try another method

provenance.evidence: Mapped from a single first-hand case, captured in interview while the case was still open. Service-level detail beyond the customer's line of sight (backstage systems, roles, KPIs) is inferred from the observed behaviour of the service rather than confirmed by the organisations involved.

researchSources.source: First-hand account of a live roadside breakdown case (notes held privately, outside version control)

governance.legalBasis: Not applicable — fictional composite for a published example set, derived from a consented first-hand account with name, bank, provider, country and dates removed.
